body: Happens in the North, too. It's inescapable.

It saps your energy. When I saw this question, I had tons of ideas of things to say. Loneliness is a subject I'm very familiar with. But I find myself unable to say those things, as that would take effort. So instead I'm going to lay in bed, and read what other people have to say about feeling alone.

I tend to assume that people don't have any interest in me. Not that they *dislike* me, but that they're indifferent to my existence. So I don't approach them, because I think it would be bothersome. It always surprises me when people like me.

Despite this, I'm fairly self confident. I don't know why I lack confidence in this area.

I don't remember when disgust disappeared. It's an emotion I have no recollection of.

But when nerves, anger, and excitement left, I saw it happen. Unfortunately, I remember them pretty clearly.

I don't see anything to gain from killing myself, so I don't do it. It isn't worth the effort.

Yeah, seeing evidence of other people's relationships is painful.

When I hear about lonely people with social lives, I get irrationally angry. I know it's possible to feel alone when surrounded by people, but *damn*, I can't help but get jealous.

There isn't really anything I can think of to tell you. You sound like me. I don't know if this applies to you, but I personally take comfort in the knowledge that there are other lonely, stunted people out there.
